incidents.name: Storage issues in us-east-1 and eu-central-1

incident_updates.body: The incident has been resolved.

The planned database capacity increase for Storage in us-east-1 was completed at 08:06 UTC. Some requests to Storage in us-east-1 may have failed briefly while the database switched over during the change. Storage in us east-1 and eu-central-1 is operating normally. We are continuing to monitor Storage error rates.

We will be conducting maintenance to address storage service improvements between 0800 and 0900 UTC on 5 November 2026. There may be an interruption of storage services in us-east-1 at some point during that window. The impact will be of a short duration and limited to us-east-1.

The cause of the issue has been identified as directly related to load. We will be doing maintenance on our platform to address this issue. As of now, storage response has returned to normal. We will continue to monitor the environment.

We are still investigating increased error rates for storage requests, and have expanded the investigation to eu-central-1 as well.

The team has identified higher-than-usual load in some areas of the storage infrastructure and is currently working on remediation options.
We have identified some customers in us-east-1 are experiencing 5XX errors when interacting with our Storage components. We are investigating.

incidents.name: Intermittent connection errors via the connection pooler in us-east-1

incident_updates.body: Between 22:10 and 22:51 UTC on October 9, 2026, about 1% of new database connections made through the Shared Pooler (Supavisor) in us-east-1 failed with "Failed to connect to database" timeout errors. The cause of the failures was an incident at our cloud provider which affected network traffic between availability zones. Supabase Project databases were not affected, and connections that had already been open prior to the incident remained open. The issue was resolved at 22:51 UTC. Clients that retried on connection errors would have reconnected successfully.
